correctness.finding: PASS. Boundary-ear insertion preserves a polygon triangulation and changes degrees exactly by (+1,+2,+1) on the affected boundary triple. Starting from the published H_k degree pattern, the displayed eighteen residue templates therefore reduce the all-orders upper bound to finite local degree-count updates; their resulting three-degree-window maxima equal ceil((4n+10)/9) for every residue. The source supplies the matching lower bound for n≥14. I independently exhaustively enumerated all convex-polygon triangulations for 5≤n≤13, reproducing the Catalan counts 5,14,42,132,429,1430,4862,16796,58786 and minima 5,5,6,6,6,6,7,7,8. The explicit 14≤n≤19 witnesses plus the ear construction cover the remaining orders.

originality.finding: PASS, with a disclosed supplementary-material residual. Caro–Škrekovski–Zarb prove the lower bound, equality for n≡2 mod 18, and only an additive-constant general upper bound; their paper explicitly describes seventeen additional caps as computer-verified over a finite covered range and says the universal formula is 'presumably' true. A current public open-problem record still lists the exact all-order formula as unresolved in that paper. The submitted contribution is therefore the uniform all-k proof from the residue templates and the complete small-order determination—not the conjectured formula or the mere existence of caps. The source supplementary files containing those caps were not independently inspected, but the source's own characterization of them as finite-range verification makes that omission a residual rather than a decisive priority blocker.

scientific_value.finding: PASS. The result closes the explicit additive-constant gap in the newest maximal-outerplanar spread theorem, proves the anticipated exact value for every n≥14, and completes the parameter for all n≥5 with exactly six small exceptions. The finite list of ear templates is also a reusable mechanism for turning one periodic extremal ladder into every residue class.
